That happens together, because a service cannot exist without a category; leaving them active would make them unfindable yet still orderable. Restoring later brings back the CATEGORY ONLY — you reactivate the services yourself, one at a time.
services.category_unarchive_confirm_body: The category alone is restored. The services inside it stay deactivated: making a service orderable again is a separate, deliberate choice you make per service.

sla_warnings.how_1: A threshold says how long a kind of wait may last — the customer's approval before the billing cutoff, a manager's check, a planned start that never started.
sla_warnings.how_2: When a wait crosses its threshold, the person whose wait it is gets a warning by email; one escalation later it reaches the level above.
sla_warnings.how_3: Changing a number applies from the next check, to running waits too — warnings already sent stay sent, and a cooldown keeps repeats quiet.
sla_warnings.how_4: Empty fields follow the platform default — you override only what you fill in.
sla_warnings.what_save: Applies from the next check, to running waits too. Nothing is recalculated backwards.
